sources.entry: cpython - Default, most widely used implementation of the Python programming language written in C.

summary.one_liner: CPython is the reference implementation of the Python programming language, written in C, distributed as source you build with configure and make.
summary.what_it_does: The README covers building the Python 3.16 alpha interpreter from source on Unix-like systems (Linux, BSD, macOS, Cygwin) using ./configure and make, with make test to run the test suite and make install to install it as python3. It describes optional build modes: --with-pydebug for debug builds, --enable-optimizations for Profile Guided Optimization (PGO, GCC or Clang), and --with-lto for Link Time Optimization. It explains installing multiple Python versions side by side using make install versus make altinstall. It points to external docs for Windows builds (PCbuild), macOS framework builds (Mac/README.rst), third-party build dependencies, the Developer Guide, and the online documentation. Licensing and copyright notices are included, and the README says the distribution contains no GPL code.
use_cases: create an optimized or debug Python build
install multiple Python versions side by side
notable: Reference implementation of the Python language, the most widely used Python interpreter
Supports Profile Guided Optimization and Link Time Optimization builds
Documented side-by-side installation of several Python versions using make altinstall
Platform-specific build guides for Windows, macOS, and Unix-like systems
caveats: Building a complete installation needs various third-party libraries that depend on platform and configure options
Not all standard library modules are buildable or usable on all platforms
Windows and macOS builds are documented in separate files rather than in this README
